title: RAW UNREVIEWED: f100v to f101r carries one botanical subject or starts a new entry
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. The already admitted Yale opening places f100v on the left with thirteen local inscription loci, a vessel and one nine-line prose paragraph; f101r on the right has botanical figures, three prose paragraphs and no local inscriptions. A complete reading might carry a named material or operation from the f100v paragraph into the first f101r paragraph, making the missing f101r captions a continuation effect. The rival begins a new, uncaptioned subject on f101r. Morgan M.652's Iris entry demonstrably continues across a physical page edge into text above a newly pictured Viola, so adjacency to the nearest drawing cannot decide either Voynich reading. This source is a layout warning, not a Voynich model or copied text. Require an independently owned botanical figure/component shared across the opening, or an overt written reference with a separately fixed meaning, before testing continuation. Freeze all f100v inscription loci and the complete four paragraphs with source boundaries and all alternate transcriptions; no free reassignment of a paragraph to a nearby plant. GDT812 already rejected the displaced-vessel caption test on f101r and does not license a missing label. Primaries: experiments/yolo/gdt812_additional_page_semantic_bridge/REPORT.md; experiments/yolo/gdt812_additional_page_semantic_bridge/src/VISUAL_LAYOUT_REVIEW.md; research_registry/proposals/laufenberg_f85r2_20260926/HISTORICAL_EXPECTATIONS_RESULT_20260927.md.

design.mechanism: A participant or material established in f100v's local labels and collective prose remains the subject of f101r's first prose record across the page turn.
design.unit: The complete thirteen f100v inscription loci, its entire nine-line paragraph, and all three complete f101r paragraphs on the already admitted facing physical leaves.
design.contrast: One cross-page subject continuation versus a new uncaptioned f101r entry; a common page theme without participant identity is a third rival.
design.prediction: A continuation reading must identify a single stable participant, retain its role through the complete f100v paragraph and f101r first paragraph, and explain any changed pictured component without a free word-sense switch. A new-entry reading requires its own source or topic at the f101r start and no unresolved f100v-dependent reference. If no independent visual or written owner can distinguish those two accounts, record missing binding and retain both.
design.prior_blockers: GDT812 gives no singular label-to-plant owner on f100v and no f101r labels; its cross-page packet is not score-ready. The Morgan Iris continuation demonstrates layout possibility only and does not bind a Voynich referent.
design.scope: Exploratory admitted-opening hypothesis only; no new image, reserve, species name, lexical value or scored relation.
